title: Open maps and proper/open coefficient squares from structural squares
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ work on their small pro-etale sites and put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ be the actual reduction/total-limit adjunction on ordinary derived categories of strict semilinear module systems, with unit $u$ and counit $e$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], using the simultaneous section constructions [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. System operations are exact inverse image $P_v$, derived direct image $S_v$ with $P_v\dashv S_v$, exact open extension $J_j\dashv P_j$, and derived tensor. All maps $v$ are separated finite type; maps denoted $p$ are proper and opens $j$ are quasi-compact [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Integral operations $A_{\rm int}$ are completed pullback and tensor, proper direct image, and localized completed-ring open extension [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-derived-direct-image, lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Inputs $K_i$ are derived-complete constructible integral complexes. Every input and intermediate system occurring in the assertion is normalized, has compatible etale-origin witnesses and constructible cohomology, and has cohomological and finite Tor amplitudes in common finite intervals [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For a basic operation $A$ write $d_A:\mathcal L A(\mathcal R K_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(K_i)$ for its defining strict reduction-tower identification, with two inputs for tensor and with $d_j$ fixed by [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Write $r_A:\mathcal R A_{\rm int}(K_i)\to A(\mathcal R K_i)$ for the canonical coefficient comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], using the specified $r_j$ for open extension. These maps and the canonical completed ringed-site structural maps are fixed independently, through the section-normalized constructions [def-sf-integral-system-operations, def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge].

For a finite typed word $B$ in these operations, write $B_{\rm int}(K_i)$ and $B(\mathcal R K_i)$ for its two evaluations. Define $r_B:\mathcal R B_{\rm int}(K_i)\to B(\mathcal R K_i)$ recursively: at a variable it is the identity, at a unary vertex $A$ it is $A(r_{\rm child})\circ r_A$, and at a tensor vertex it is $(r_{\rm left}\otimes r_{\rm right})\circ r_\otimes$. Coefficient unit objects have their canonical scalar-unit identification. These are finite words in the typed domain [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain], with no compact-support constructor.

Assume that the coefficient squares for tensor constraints, pullback composition, direct-image composition, and the units and counits of $P_v\dashv S_v$ and $J_j\dashv P_j$ commute on every intermediate used below. Here the coefficient square for $a:B\to C$ means $a_{\mathcal R K_i}\circ r_B=r_C\circ\mathcal R(a_{\rm int})$, using the corresponding canonical completed ringed-site map $a_{\rm int}$.

Let $Q$ be a commutative square $pk=ir$ with $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$ quasi-compact open, $r:U\to W$ and $p:V\to Z$ proper; no cartesianness is required. Put $V_W=V\times_ZW$, with projections $b:V_W\to V$, $q:V_W\to W$, and clopen lift $s=(k,r):U\to V_W$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]. Define $\lambda_Q:P_iS_pJ_k\xrightarrow{\sim}S_r$ to be the specified four-factor composite: right-adjoint conjugation of $P_pJ_i\cong J_bP_q$, followed by $S_q$ of $P_bJ_k\cong J_s$, followed by the clopen identification $J_s\cong S_s$, followed by $S_qS_s\cong S_r$. The clopen map is the $P_s\dashv S_s$ unit followed by the inverse open unit. Define $\Gamma_Q:J_iS_r\to S_pJ_k$ to be the $J_i\dashv P_i$ adjunct of $\lambda_Q^{-1}$, i.e. $J_iS_r\xrightarrow{J_i\lambda_Q^{-1}}J_iP_iS_pJ_k\xrightarrow{\epsilon^o}S_pJ_k$. Let $\lambda_{Q,\rm int},\Gamma_{Q,\rm int}$ be the same composites and open transpose of canonical completed ringed-site maps [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. Then, first, the coefficient square commutes for the canonical open base-change isomorphism $\beta:P_gJ_j\cong J_{j'}P_{g_U}$ of a cartesian square of a quasi-compact open $j$ along a map $g$, and for the open-tensor isomorphism $\gamma:J_jM\otimes N\cong J_j(M\otimes P_jN)$, each together with its inverse, where $\beta,\gamma$ and their integral counterparts $\beta_{\rm int},\gamma_{\rm int}$ carry the open-unit normalizations of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Second,
$$\lambda_{Q,\mathcal R K}\circ r_{P_iS_pJ_k}=r_{S_r}\circ\mathcal R(\lambda_{Q,\rm int}),\qquad
\Gamma_{Q,\mathcal R K}\circ r_{J_iS_r}=r_{S_pJ_k}\circ\mathcal R(\Gamma_{Q,\rm int}).$$
The intermediate systems in the four-factor composite, including words of length four, satisfy the normalization, origin and common amplitude hypotheses above; only the generator endpoints have the length-three restriction. All equalities are of whole-system morphisms before evaluation and are natural in $K$.

proof.text: Use the ambient normalized pullback-square equation, open mate invertibility and the generic inverse-adjunct transport to obtain the ambient beta square. Cancel the actual short-word completion maps and use naturality of beta to obtain its recursive-word coefficient square.

Use the restriction/tensor coefficient equation and the open-unit mate equation to transport the normalized inverse projection adjunct. Naturality and cancellation of the short-word completion maps give the open-tensor coefficient square.

Use the inverse proper/open restriction coefficient equation. For lambda cancel the reduction of inverse ringed lambda, and cancel the primitive pullback completion unit. For Gamma use the generic inverse-mate transpose formula and the recursive open comparison. This proves the two different endpoint squares without imposing a length-three bound on the additional restriction of the proper target.

Reproduce the published short-word completion induction as a private helper from primitive completion effectivity and the short-word integral domain, avoiding the parent coherence import. For beta, gamma and lambda, the independent system and ringed generator maps are isomorphisms. Their integral maps are conjugates through invertible endpoint completion maps. Multiply the forward square by the two inverses to get the inverse square. Prove input naturality by induction on words: naturality of tensor, pullback, direct image and open comparison combines the child equations. Naturality of completion transports gives naturality of the integral generator maps. Case analysis on the four OpenGenerator constructors assembles all clauses.

It is a first split (no proof on base, no re-split note, not dropped), with nine steps, no new nodes, statement and metadata unchanged and proof_deps equal to the union of the uses. I checked each step's formula and domains against the cited statements. Step 2: beta^{-1} = eps∘J_{j'}(theta^{-1}∘F_U u°) matches lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization; theta is a pullback compositor. Step 3: the restriction/tensor square, the only content outside the hypotheses (the sibling tensor-adjunction-squares node does not include pullback monoidality), is fixed by def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison (first Roos coordinate (1⊗x)⊗(1⊗y), shifted coordinate 0), lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison (completed = ordinary restriction for an immersion) and site-derived-tensor-descent; I accept it. Step 4: the gamma^{-1} adjunct matches the normalization node. Step 5: d^{-1} is the inverse-mate formula with the roles of the two adjunctions swapped (checked against def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate); z: P_bJ_k→J_s is correct because b^{-1}(U) = U×_Z W ≅ U via s. Step 6: c is exactly the conjugate of beta^{-1} for P_pJ_i ⊣ P_iS_p and J_bP_q ⊣ S_qP_b. Step 7: h_s is unit then inverse open unit, as the statement pins it. Steps 8 and 9: lambda is cJ_k, S_q z, S_q h_s, a_{q,s} with qs = r, matching the factors in lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting; Gamma is the open transpose of lambda^{-1}. Small cases: j = id, U empty, a noncartesian Q with an extra component of V_W, and s clopen because qs = r is proper and q separated. No duplicate found in the snapshot DAG. The two declared tool uses are on the unit's route through sec-smooth-purity and sec-proper-base-change; I accept them. No SGA source is cited. theorem openInterchangeReductionSquares
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} (C : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] (o : Operations C.l E)
    (_hStructural : StructuralSquares.{u, s, i} C.l E D o)
    {S : Type s} (W : S → Scheme.{u}) (_hW : FiniteTypeFamily W D.k)
    {I : Type i} (location : I → S)
    {a : S} {B Cw : Word W location a} (g : GeneratorKind W location B Cw)
    (_hOpen : OpenGenerator g) (_hB : B.length ≤ 3) (_hC : Cw.length ≤ 3)
    (K : ∀ k : I, DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource C.l E (W (location k))))
    (lo hi torLo torHi : ℤ)
    (_hAdm : ∀ k : I, Admissible C.l E
      (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus C.l E (W (location k))) (K k)
      lo hi torLo torHi)
    (_hIntermediate : Word.admissible C.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi B ∧
      Word.admissible C.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi Cw)
    (_hGenerator : g.admissible C.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi) :
    Assertion C.l E W location o K g ∧
      (OpenIsomorphism g →
        IsIso (g.systemMap C.l E W location o (inputReduction C.l E W location K)) ∧
        IsIso (g.integralMap C.l E W location o K) ∧
        InverseAssertion C.l E W location o K g) ∧
      (∀ (L : ∀ k : I, DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource C.l E (W (location k)))),
        (∀ k : I, Admissible C.l E
          (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus C.l E (W (location k))) (L k)
          lo hi torLo torHi) →
        Word.admissible C.l E W location o L lo hi torLo torHi B →
        Word.admissible C.l E W location o L lo hi torLo torHi Cw →
        g.admissible C.l E W location o L lo hi torLo torHi →
        ∀ f : ∀ k : I, K k ⟶ L k, SquareNaturality C.l E W location o f g)
